title: ApplicationDetail codec round-trip exercises only the new-field defaults (reference_calls: [], attestation_on_file: False)
detail: Both ApplicationDetail round-trip tests pass only the optional_field defaults; a non-empty reference_calls entry and attestation_on_file:true never traverse encode→decoder. A wrong envelope wiring (e.g. missing decode.list) would pass CI and break production decoding of real payloads.
recommended_fix: Add a third application_detail_codec round-trip carrying one populated ReferenceCallDetail plus attestation_on_file: True, asserting the exact record comes back.

title: Attempt-log writer/reader shape agreement is untested — wire test asserts only the "attempts" key, and the strict shared decoder would silently drop the whole log
evidence:
129:  string.contains(body, "\"attempts\"") |> should.be_true

shared/src/shared/reference_call.gleam:
  use at <- decode.field("at", decode.string)
  use channel <- decode.field("channel", decode.string)
  use outcome <- decode.field("outcome", decode.string)
  use detail <- decode.field("detail", decode.string)

reference_checks_integration_test.gleam:284-286 (the append API accepts a 3-key entry):
      #("at", json.string("2026-07-31T22:00:00Z")),
      #("channel", json.string("email")),
      #("outcome", json.string("sent")),
detail: If the stored attempts text ever fails the strict shared decoder (any entry missing one of the four keys, e.g. detail), decode.list fails and parse_attempt_log degrades to [] — the panel silently shows an empty log. The integration test's key-presence assertion stays green either way, so no test pins the writer/reader agreement.
recommended_fix: Assert a decoded attempt's content on the wire (e.g. escaped "\"channel\": \"email\"") in the strip test, or unit-test a sweep-built outcome_entry round-tripping through shared attempt_decoder.

title: No cross-tenant negative test for the new reference_calls/attestation read paths (GET detail has no foreign-landlord test at all)
detail: All six new integration tests seed a single landlord; every existing handle_get_detail test likewise uses the owner. The new privacy-sensitive reads are gated only by the pre-existing landlord-scoped outer query, and nothing pins that a foreign landlord gets 404/no reference data.
recommended_fix: Seed landlord_b and assert handle_get_detail returns 404 (or an empty reference_calls) when landlord_a requests landlord_b's application.
